holidays.name: National Toasted Marshmallow Day
holidays.description: A day for sticking a marshmallow on a stick and holding it over a fire until it turns golden brown, or charred black if that's your style. It's a good excuse for a late-summer campfire, a backyard fire pit, s'mores, or just a gooey snack.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance that falls at the end of summer, when campfire season is winding down. The marshmallow itself goes back to ancient Egypt, where the sweet sap of the mallow plant was made into a treat for gods and royalty. The fluffy modern version appeared in the 19th century.
holidays.funFact: The original marshmallow treats were made from the sap of the marsh mallow plant, which grows in wetlands. That plant is where the name comes from.

holidays.name: National Slinky Day
holidays.description: A celebration of the springy toy that walks down stairs, stretches across the room, and gets tangled beyond repair. Dig out a Slinky, find a staircase, and watch it flip end over end.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It honors the Slinky, which grew out of a lucky accident. Naval engineer Richard James was working with tension springs in the early 1940s when one fell off a shelf and tumbled across the floor instead of landing in a heap. He turned the idea into a toy.
holidays.funFact: The first Slinkys went on sale in a Philadelphia department store in 1945. The roughly 400 on display reportedly sold out in about 90 minutes.
